successCriteria.description: calculateBusinessDays returns the correct count of business days (Monday–Friday) within an inclusive [startDate, endDate] range, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and any date whose calendar date matches an entry in the holidays array.
calculateBusinessDays returns 1 when startDate and endDate are the same calendar day that falls on a business day (not a weekend or holiday).
calculateBusinessDays returns 0 when startDate is after endDate (inverted range), without throwing.
getHolidaysForYear queries the holidays table via the pg pool, filtering by the given year and country = 'US', and returns an array of Date objects derived from the date column.
Both calculateBusinessDays and getHolidaysForYear are exported through the barrel at src/shared/utils/index.ts and are importable from that path.
Unit tests in tests/unit/shared/utils/ cover: weekends excluded, holidays excluded, same-day = 1, multi-day spans, and inverted-range edge cases, and all pass under npx jest.
npm run build completes with no TypeScript compilation errors and npx jest --passWithNoTests exits zero.

constraints: calculateBusinessDays must be a pure function with no database access and no side effects — it must not import or call the pool.

Date comparison in calculateBusinessDays must compare only the calendar date (year/month/day) of each day in the range against the holidays array; time components must be ignored to avoid false negatives.

No use of the `any` type anywhere in the utility or its tests — use `unknown` with type guards or `Record<string, unknown>` with explicit casts, consistent with the existing repository mapRow pattern.
getHolidaysForYear must use parameterized SQL (pool.query with $1/$2 placeholders) — no string-interpolated values in the query — matching the existing repository query style.
The holidays table query must filter by country = 'US' as the default; the function signature takes only a year parameter and does not expose a country parameter.
Whole days only — no half-day or partial-day counting logic is permitted in this utility.
This utility is the single source of truth for leave day-count calculations; no other code path may independently compute business-day counts for balance sufficiency, deduction, or restoration.
outOfScope: The leave service (Phase 9) that consumes calculateBusinessDays and getHolidaysForYear for balance sufficiency checks, deduction, and restoration is out of scope for this phase.
Database migrations or schema creation for the holidays table are out of scope — the utility assumes the table already exists with columns date, name, and country.
Support for country parameters other than the default 'US' is out of scope — the function signature is fixed to year-only.
Half-day or partial-day leave counting is out of scope — whole days only.
Caching of holiday query results is out of scope for this phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: For any valid inclusive date range where startDate <= endDate, the returned count is always >= 0 and equals the number of days in the range that are Monday–Friday and not present in the holidays array (by calendar date). The function never throws for any Date inputs.
The function always returns a Promise that resolves to a Date[] (possibly empty) and never returns undefined; if the query yields no rows, an empty array is returned.

interfaceConstraints.operation: calculateBusinessDays(startDate: Date, endDate: Date, holidays: Date[]): number
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Must not throw for any input, including inverted ranges (startDate > endDate returns 0) and dates with arbitrary time components.
If the underlying pool.query rejects, the rejection propagates to the caller (no silent swallowing); an empty result set resolves to an empty array, not null or undefined.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: getHolidaysForYear must obtain the pg Pool from the same export used by all existing repositories — the `pool` named export — so connection configuration is shared and not duplicated.
The barrel export at src/shared/utils/index.ts must follow the same simple re-export style used by existing module barrels (e.g., `export { X, Y } from './file'`).

getHolidaysForYear must use parameterized SQL via pool.query(sql, params) with a mapRow-style conversion from the raw DB row to the return type, matching the established repository pattern for snake_case-to-camelCase mapping and Record<string, unknown> casting.

Unit tests must mock the pool using the same pattern as existing repository tests: jest.mock('shared/db/connection', () => ({ pool: { query: jest.fn() } })) with mockReset() in beforeEach, resolving via the jest.config.js moduleDirectories and tsconfig baseUrl.

integrationPoints.why: getHolidaysForYear queries the holidays table through the shared pg Pool; this is the runtime dependency for holiday data retrieval.

The leave service will be the primary consumer, calling getHolidaysForYear(fiscalYear) then calculateBusinessDays(startDate, endDate, holidays) for balance sufficiency checks, deduction on submit, and restoration on reject/cancel.
getHolidaysForYear reads from the holidays table (columns: date, name, country) to supply the holiday list consumed by calculateBusinessDays.
